# Kotter Inc. — Narrative & Copy Research (2025–2026)

## Name + What It Is
**Dr. John P. Kotter** (Harvard Business School professor, author of *Leading Change*) and **Kotter International Inc. ("Kotter Inc.")**, the change-leadership consulting and training firm built on his research. The flagship methodology is **"The 8-Step Process for Leading Change"** (originally framed as the "8 Accelerators" for continuous, agile change). Positioned as consulting + certification/training.

**Buyer they talk to:** C-suite and senior enterprise leaders (CEOs, COOs, executives, transformation offices) at large organizations across healthcare, pharma, manufacturing, utilities, consumer products, and government. The frame is "we do transformation *with* you," i.e., leaders driving org-wide change.

## Primary URLs
- Home: https://www.kotterinc.com
- 8-Step Process: https://www.kotterinc.com/methodology/8-steps/
- Science of Change: https://www.kotterinc.com/methodology/the-science-of-change/
- About: https://www.kotterinc.com/about-us/
- AI course (2026): https://www.kotterinc.com/learning-development/ai-course/
- Thriving Through Uncertainty: https://www.kotterinc.com/thriving-through-uncertainty-course/

## Narrative / Story Frame
The story: **the world faces accelerating, threatening change; human beings are biologically wired to hunker down and resist it; great leadership flips that response from fear into opportunity, mobilizing masses of people to change fast.** Two proprietary lenses carry the emotional/strategic angle:

1. **"Survive and Thrive"** (the neuroscience layer) — change triggers a hardwired survival/threat response that must be turned into an opportunity ("Thrive") response.
2. **"Head + Heart"** — change requires both rational (head) and emotional (heart) engagement; data and logic alone don't move people.

The 2025–2026 overlay is **AI and uncertainty**: reframing anxiety about AI-era disruption as the "big opportunity."

## Verbatim Copy (exact quotes)

**Homepage:**
- "Change Leadership + Transformation Reimagined."
- "The evidence is overwhelming. The world is facing more change and uncertainty."
- "Lead Change in the AI Era."
- "Turn Anxiety into Adaptability."
- "Millions Leading, Billions Benefiting"
- "We do transformation with you, not for you or to you."
- "Together, we create a movement."
- "We pioneered the Science of Change."
- "There's a better way to change."

**8-Step page:**
- "Kotter's award-winning methodology is the proven approach to producing lasting change"
- Step 1 — "Create A Sense of Urgency": "Inspire people to act – with passion and purpose – to achieve a bold, aspirational opportunity."
- Step 2 — "Build A Guiding Coalition": "A volunteer network needs a coalition of committed people – born of its own ranks – to guide it, coordinate it, and communicate its activities."
- Step 3 — "Form A Strategic Vision": "Clarify how the future will be different from the past and get buy-in for how you can make that future a reality."
- Step 4 — "Enlist A Volunteer Army": "Large-scale change can only occur when massive numbers of people rally around a common opportunity."
- Step 5 — "Enable Action By Removing Barriers": "Remove the obstacles that slow things down or create roadblocks to progress."
- Step 6 — "Generate Short-Term Wins": "Wins are the molecules of results. They must be recognized, collected, and communicated."
- Step 7 — "Sustain Acceleration": "Press harder after the first successes."
- Step 8 — "Institute Change": "Articulate the connections between new behaviors and organizational success."

**Science of Change page:**
- "The Human Hardwired Response to Change"
- "Evolution has resulted in a two-channel system – Survive and Thrive – which influences how we respond to threats and opportunities."
- "The vast majority of people tend to seriously underestimate the power of our built-in survival instinct and how it can, inadvertently, overwhelm our capacity to see opportunities, innovate, adapt, lead, and change for the better."
- "Why do some organizations outperform others? Why do some individual managers and executives produce so much more?"

**About page:**
- Mission: "Kotter's mission is to guide, educate, and inspire people so that they can become significantly better leaders, successfully transform organizations into truly great enterprises, and build a better world for future generations."
- Vision: "Millions leading, billions benefiting."
- Origin: "Our story begins with an opportunity. In our case, it was the belief Dr. John Kotter held that if more people were better leaders, the benefits would be endless."
- "We challenge ourselves like we challenge our clients – stubborn in the belief that so much more is possible."
- "By teaching others to transform their organizations, we create more leadership from more people – unlocking the potential for a thriving world."

**2026 course copy (Leading Change in the Era of AI):**
- Leverages "the science of Survive + Thrive to shift your workforce from reluctant compliance to genuine commitment."

## "Head + Heart" / "Behavior" language
- Confirmed a **core principle "Head + Heart"** (rational + emotional engagement) appears across Kotter's Science-of-Change and course materials (e.g., the "Selling Your Case for Change" course). It's referenced as a named pillar but isn't rendered as a standalone hero string on the Science-of-Change page itself.
- The "change happens by changing behavior" idea surfaces verbatim in **Step 8**: *"Articulate the connections between **new behaviors** and organizational success."*
- The classic Kotter tension of **"have to" vs "want to"** ("build excitement around the Big Opportunity and develop a feeling that one 'wants to' contribute") appears in Kotter's downloadable eBooks (e.g., the *8 Steps to Accelerate Change* PDF) rather than the current page heroes.

## Dominant Recurring Words / Phrases
change · transformation · "Science of Change" · urgency · "big opportunity" / "opportunity" · movement · mobilize / "volunteer army" · leadership · adaptability / agility · "Survive and Thrive" · "Head + Heart" · uncertainty · AI era · "with you, not for you or to you" · "millions leading, billions benefiting" · acceleration · behaviors · results / "short-term wins".

# McKinsey — Change / Transformation Practice: Narrative & Positioning Research

## 1. Name + What It Is
- **McKinsey Transformation** — the firm's dedicated transformation practice. Positioned as helping clients achieve "full potential" performance change at pace.
- **The Influence Model** — McKinsey's four-part change-management framework for shifting mindsets and behavior. Introduced in the McKinsey Quarterly article "The psychology of change management" (Tessa Basford & Bill Schaninger, 11 Apr 2016), later reframed as "The four building blocks of change."
- Four building blocks: **role modeling; fostering understanding and conviction; reinforcing with formal mechanisms; developing talent and skills.**
- Firm-level banner: **"Change that Matters."**

## 2. Primary URLs
- Transformation practice hub: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/transformation
- How we help clients: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/transformation/how-we-help-clients
- Change that Matters: https://www.mckinsey.com/about-us/overview/change-that-matters
- The four building blocks of change (Influence Model): https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/people-and-organizational-performance/our-insights/the-four-building-blocks--of-change
- Why do most transformations fail? (Harry Robinson): https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/transformation/our-insights/why-do-most-transformations-fail-a-conversation-with-harry-robinson
- Chief Transformation Officers: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/transformation/how-we-help-clients/chief-transformation-officers
- Ability to Execute: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/transformation/how-we-help-clients/ability-to-execute

## 3. Narrative / Story Frame (verbatim)
The core story is **failure → human side → performance + health**.

- **The failure hook:** "The academic research is really clear that when corporations launch transformations, roughly 70 percent fail." (Harry Robinson)
- **Root cause = the leader's conviction/narrative:** in the early stages the CEO often doesn't "build conviction within the team about the importance of this change or craft a change narrative that convinces people they need to make the transformation happen."
- **Human side:** transformation "requires individuals to behave differently," so leaders must address "how people think and act in their day-to-day work"; the differentiator is "the involvement of frontline employees and their managers."
- **The "why":** organizations "fail to attach a compelling 'why?' to their effort" — at-scale change requires "thousands of employees choose to get on board with new ways of working," and "simply protecting the bottom line isn't sufficient motivation."
- **Performance + health:** beyond performance and growth, leaders "must also address culture, mind-sets, and the company's organizational health."

## 4. Verbatim Taglines & Positioning Copy
- **"Change that Matters."** (headline banner)
- **"McKinsey creates Change that Matters through transformation, enabled by technology, and sustained through capabilities."** (the three-pillar positioning line)
- Firm mission line reused in transformation framing: **"help our clients make distinctive, lasting, and substantial improvements in their performance."**
- Practice promise: McKinsey "gives clients the confidence to aim high," turning "bold strategies into reality — all at a pace they didn't think possible."
- Ambition framing: push for **"far-reaching ambition beyond performance improvement to unlock an organization's full potential"**; "engage and energize people across an entire business"; "drive execution and track impact at a relentless pace."
- **Ability to Execute** = "a suite of programs designed to equip leaders and teams with the skills, mindsets, and behaviors required to drive and sustain performance at scale."
- On capability: **"Capability gaps are one of the greatest barriers to successful transformation."**

Influence Model definitional lines (verbatim):
- The framework focuses on "four key actions to change mindsets and behavior: fostering understanding and conviction, reinforcing changes through formal mechanisms, developing talent and skills, and role modeling."
- Proof points cited: those who "fostered understanding and conviction are 3.2 times more likely… to report outperformance"; where "leaders role modeled changes" they are "1.6 times more likely to report outperforming their peers."

## 5. Who They Talk To (the buyer)
Top-of-house: **CEOs, the C-suite, and boards.**
- "McKinsey helps CEOs unlock the full potential of transformations to drive outsize performance."
- "CEOs must aim high to unlock an organization's full potential."
- The CEO is framed as owner of the change narrative; the practice also sells the **Chief Transformation Officer (CTO)** role: "the most successful transformation programs feature a strong Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) at the center," "empowered to drive the company toward its full potential."

## 6. Dominant Recurring Words / Phrases
full potential · aim high · mindsets and behavior(s) · at scale · performance and health · role modeling · understanding and conviction · reinforcement mechanisms · capabilities / capability building · relentless pace · change narrative · sustained / enduring · outperform peers · Change that Matters.

**Emotional/strategic angle:** rational-emotional blend — a fear hook (70% fail) resolved by ambition ("aim high," "full potential") and the human/psychological lever (conviction, role modeling, a compelling "why"), all anchored to hard performance proof (outperformance multipliers). Sober, evidence-led, C-suite-flattering.
